thread:
Ashley: quick heads-up — I opened a vuln triage for the KMS client libs (CVE-style finding). Fuzzing hit an unwrap edge that can return a malformed DEK header. Not exploitable in our infra yet but felt worth discussing rotation + mitigations. @jonathan @maya
Jonathan: thanks. can you paste the fuzz log? curious if it's parsing only or leads to a wrong-key unwrap path
Ashley: log pasted in the ticket — gist link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/kms-unwrap-fuzz — short version: malformed header leads to a nil DEK id, client treats as cache miss and calls KMS, sometimes retries without backoff.
Maya: oof. that retry behavior could amplify KMS calls under fuzz or malformed input -> think rate limit risk, cost spike. Also audit noise.
Ashley: exactly. proposed immediate steps: 1) tighten parsing (reject absent dek_id), 2) add client-side replay/fuzz filter for malformed envelopes, 3) reduce DEK caching TTL for untrusted callers, 4) emergency KEK rotation plan if needed. thoughts?
Jonathan: +1 to parsing fix and rejecting. For caching TTL: we should differentiate by caller identity. For internal, authenticated service-to-service we can keep DEK cache TTL longer (e.g., 5m). For public/untrusted, drop to 15s and apply jitter/splay. Also add circuit-breaker to avoid thundering herd to KMS.
Priya: RBAC note — create a dedicated KMS principal for the decrypt path with a narrowly scoped policy: kms:Decrypt + kms:GenerateDataKey (where needed) only from the specific service account. No key creation or rotation perms. For GCP/Azure equivalents: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter limited to resource path.
Maya: Audit logging: ensure CloudTrail / Audit Logs include principal and request context; forward to SIEM. Add an alert for >X decrypt calls per minute per principal. Also log envelope metadata (dek_id, key_id, envelope_version) but never log plaintext or raw ciphertext.
Jonathan: re: KMS call frequency and caching strategy: suggested pattern we use elsewhere — cache DEK in an in-memory LRU + pinned hot-key entry, TTL default 5m for internal, 30s for external. Add a small HMAC-based proof on envelope to detect replay/malformation before hitting cache. HMAC key derived from DEK: we can verify integrity without calling KMS.
Ashley: thinking about robustness if KEK compromised: offline rewrap path. approach: when rotating KEK, create new KEK in KMS, call a background rewrap job that fetches encrypted DEKs, calls KMS to rewrap (or decrypt+generate) and write back. But for very large blob counts, we should support lazy rewrap on read (read -> rewrap if dek_version < current) plus a bulk job for hot data.
Priya: Azure nuance — Key Vault supports update and key rotation but you also get a key-version id; use that to tag envelopes. For GCP use cryptoKeyVersions similarly. Key id in envelope must be authoritative.
Maya: operational matters: implement splayed TTL + jitter (rand(0, TTL/3)) to reduce simultaneous expiry across hosts. And exponential backoff + capped retries for KMS calls. Encryptor-bot: deployed a small client patch to validate envelope header fields and add splay. Patch ready for canary.
encryptor-bot: DEPLOY BOT: canary rolled to 3 pods in eu-west-1 at 2468135830, health OK, no spike in KMS ops.
Jonathan: for incident response — runbook items: 1) isolate offending service identity if we see abnormal unwrap failures, 2) revoke KMS key policy binding for suspect principal, 3) trigger KEK rotate (create new key version), 4) enable rewrap job, 5) notify customers if data exposure risk. Keep communications typed as security incident.
Ashley: vuln triage notes: mark severity medium for now (exploitable only with malformed envelope supply). Remediation ETA: parsing harden + canary client patch today, wider rollout tomorrow, RBAC least-privileges in next sprint.
Maya: one more ask — add a small local metric: envelope_malformed_rate, increment before any KMS call. Alert if >0.1% over 5m window. That helps spot fuzz/replay attacks early.
Priya: I'll open the IAM PR to create the restricted decrypt principal + add IAM conditions to limit network origin.
Ashley: thanks all. will update the ticket with rollback/rotate runbook and assign follow-ups. :thumbsup:
